claim: Initial apical displacement and C-initial cluster formation have distinct segmental domains; equal vowels or low V2 yield long V1, unequal high V2 can yield a short outcome.
status: Tested against182 manually annotated formations covering every117 Telugu D-bearing family; strict surface quantity results25/33 long,8/8 differing-high short,21/21 consonantal short. Conditional/mixed inputs excluded.
test: Use independent V1,V2,apical,C1 and syllable/morphological input annotations, never fit V2 to observed output.

claim: Later CR cluster simplification loses R in Telugu but can lose C1 in other SCDr languages, especially initial n,w,s.
status: Tested across409 comparative entries: visible cluster/reduced doublets support concealment, but direct medial assimilation remains an alternative for r-less forms without cluster witnesses. Telugu vrāyu>rāyu is a first-member-loss exception to a uniform Telugu R-loss formula.
test: Separate visible metathesis, historically attested clusters and only inferred hidden outcomes; verify dated/dialect clusters.

source: Krishnamurti 2003 pp.115–117; Kekunnaya 1994 pp.42–44 quoted there
claim: Recent SD I initial-vowel loss, especially in Tulu/Irula, need not be historically shared with SCDr metathesis.
status: Primary K03 source and source-labeled DEDR variants inspected; Kekunnaya full source not obtained
test: Compare vowel survival, quantity and dialect restrictions; do not count every initial liquid as the same event.

claim: The derivation of Telugu davvu and Naikri dhāv from *iṭ-a is questioned.
status: Primary text inspected, d446 marked ambiguous
test: Check aspirated recipient forms, possible alternative ancestry and exact historical vowels; no unsupported a-reconstruction.

claim: Later Kuvi metathesis targets closed-syllable sonorants; earlier VLV reduction supplied initial-liquid patterns. Nasals were added to the domain.
status: Full final PDF obtained; pp.225–226 images checked
test: Audit nasal plurals and lexical doublets separately from older initial-vowel contraction. The proposed perceptual motivation is not established by dictionary correspondences alone.

source: Hume 2004 pp.225–226 reporting Krishnamurti1978 and Israel1979
claim: Published counts: Kui98 and Kuvi59 changed forms, plus19/23 variable forms; Kuvi open/closed initial-syllable text frequencies1535/736.
status: Verified as Hume’s reporting; underlying K78 and Israel full sources not yet obtained
test: Do not claim replication or compare token-frequency denominators with database lexical-type counts.

claim: Stem-final velar plus labial verbal formative surfaces in reversed order; nonvelar controls retain their order. The suffix is not uniformly causative.
status: All152 literal-screen records adjudicated. Supported-family counts Kui61/61,Kuvi2/3 with one possible retained source variant,Pengo4/4,Manda2/2; additional55 source paradigm observations preserve nonvelar and vowel-stem controls.
test: 152 screen records include 61 Kui source-supported verbal families, nominal and labial-stem pk controls, and Kuvi Schulze kakpinai as a possible retained counterexample. Garrett and Blevins2009 analogical-origin hypothesis remains distinct from synchronic regularity.

claim: Source-attributed first-quarter seventh-century initial-ḻ destroy at Potladurti, independent670–680 witness, and890 coexisting full/displaced formations.
status: Fourteen historical observations exported with separate source dating, written reading and inferred sound history. Earlier first-quarter seventh-century claim is source-attributed, not an absolute onset date.
test: Differentiate relative chronology, source-attributed dates and nonidentical morphological contexts; one root regardless of token count.

claim: Older native metathesis ceased as an active formative principle in Middle Telugu while literary doublets and distinct sporadic/loan metatheses persisted.
test: Test actual grammatical formations and dated texts; neither coexisting doublets nor1290 Druggādēvi alone demonstrate continuous productivity.

source: Garrett and Blevins2009 pp.537–543, §22.4; p.538 image checked
claim: Kondh kp/pk and gb/bg alternations may arise from causative replacement, reinterpretation, plural-action double marking and analogical generalization rather than a phonetic KP>PK sound change.
status: Source paradigms and labial/vowel-base controls establish nonexchange routes to pk. They make the analogical account viable but do not uniquely establish its reconstructed historical sequence.
test: Winfield73 vowel-final bases with strengthened -p plus -ki and database labial-base pk derivatives establish a nonmetathetic source of pk. These support possibility, not unique historical proof.

source: Hume2002 p.38 ex.38 versus Winfield1928 p.72 and DEDR1080

status: Both page images checked; DEDR kapka confirms labial infinitive in laugh

claim: Schulze/Fitzgerald transcriptions can be inaccurate; Bisamkatak consultant resident in Kui area may show contact effects.
status: Introductory p.231 read; attempted local full-PDF extraction failed because the saved file was an HTML access page. Full article not consulted. Source/dialect caveat retained without deleting contrary evidence.
test: Preserve source/dialect labels; neither source criticism nor possible contact licenses automatic deletion of kakpinai or treating every Bisamkatak feature as borrowed.

claim: Lowering distribution and relative chronology distinguish vowels produced by different contractions.
status: All25 numbered positive/control/exception items audited; printed-list Kui17/18 selected or17/17 explicitly nonmissing, Kuvi9/18, Manda2/18. Exact inherited low-a formation is independently supported in only a subset.
test: No population estimate from the selected list; preserved open-mid quality is a historical hypothesis, not a look-back rule.
